Hemigrammus bleheri.title: Petitella bleheri, Firehead tetra : fisheries, aquarium
Hemigrammus bleheri.ecology: Freshwater; benthopelagic; pH range: 5.0 - 6.0; dH range: 5 - 12. Tropical; 23°C - 26°C (Ref. 1672 )
Hemigrammus bleheri.distribution: | Faunafri South America: Negro and Meta River basins.

Gymnocorymbus ternetzi.title: Gymnocorymbus ternetzi, Black tetra : fisheries, aquarium
Gymnocorymbus ternetzi.ecology: Freshwater; pelagic; pH range: 6.0 - 8.0; dH range: 5 - 19. Subtropical; 20°C - 26°C (Ref. 1672 ); 11°S - 30°S, 64°W - 48°W
Gymnocorymbus ternetzi.distribution: | Faunafri South America: Paraguay and Guaporé River basins to Argentina (Ref. 9086 ).
Gymnocorymbus ternetzi.biology: Adults occur in the middle and upper water layers. They feed on worms, small crustaceans and insects (Ref. 7020 ). Migratory behaviour is undetermined (Ref. 126106 ). Aquarium keeping: in groups of 5 or more individuals; minimum aquarium size 60 cm (Ref. 51150 ).

Hyphessobrycon amandae.title: Hyphessobrycon amandae, Ember tetra : fisheries, aquarium
Hyphessobrycon amandae.distribution: | Faunafri South America: Araguaia River basin.

Pterophyllum scalare.title: Pterophyllum scalare, Freshwater angelfish : fisheries, aquarium
Pterophyllum scalare.ecology: Freshwater; benthopelagic; pH range: 6.0 - 8.0; dH range: 5 - 13; non-migratory (Ref. 126106 ). Tropical; 24°C - 30°C (Ref. 40602 ); 6°N - 10°S, 78°W - 51°W
Pterophyllum scalare.distribution: | Faunafri South America: Amazon River basin, in Peru, Colombia, and Brazil, along the Ucayali, Solimões and Amazon rivers; rivers of Amapá (Brazil), Rio Oyapock in French Guiana; Essequibo River in Guyana.
Pterophyllum scalare.biology: Adults inhabit swamps or flooded grounds where the aquatic and riverine vegetation are dense and the water is either clear or silty. Its color is deeper in clear water (Ref. 35237 ). One of the most popular of all the tropical aquarium fish. Maximum length 15 cm TL (Ref. 7020 ). Aquarium keeping: in groups of 5 or more individuals; keep pairs in small tanks for breeding; minimum aquarium size 100 cm (Ref. 51539 ).

Symphysodon discus.title: Symphysodon discus, Red discus : fisheries, aquarium
Symphysodon discus.ecology: Freshwater; benthopelagic; pH range: 4.2 - 6.2; dH range: 0 - 1; non-migratory (Ref. 126106 ). Tropical; 26°C - 30°C (Ref. 1672 ); 1°S - 3°S
Symphysodon discus.distribution: | Faunafri South America: Amazon River basin in Brazil, near the mouth of the Negro River, in the lower Abacaxis River, and in the lower Trombetas River.
Symphysodon discus.biology: They feed on worms, crustaceans, insects and plant matter. Maximum length 20 cm TL (Ref. 7020 ).

Mikrogeophagus ramirezi.title: Mikrogeophagus ramirezi, Ram cichlid : aquarium
Mikrogeophagus ramirezi.ecology: Freshwater; benthopelagic; pH range: 5.0 - 6.0; dH range: 5 - 12; non-migratory. Tropical; 27°C - 30°C (Ref. 30491 )
Mikrogeophagus ramirezi.distribution: | Faunafri South America: Orinoco River basin, in the llanos of Venezuela and Colombia.
Mikrogeophagus ramirezi.biology: Used in behavioral studies (Ref. 4537 ). Aquarium keeping: in pairs; minimum aquarium size 60 cm (Ref. 51539 ).

Betta splendens.title: Betta splendens, Siamese fighting fish : aquarium
Betta splendens.ecology: Freshwater; benthopelagic; pH range: 6.0 - 8.0; dH range: 5 - 19. Tropical; 24°C - 30°C (Ref. 1672 ); 22°N - 8°N, 99°E - 107°E
Betta splendens.biology: Facultative air-breathing (Ref. 126274 ); Occur in standing waters of floodplains, canals, rice paddies (Ref. 12693 ) and medium to large rivers (Ref. 12975 ). Feed on zooplankton, mosquito and other insect larvae (Ref. 12693 ). Air breather and bubble nest builder. Used in behavioral studies (Ref. 4537 ). Males will fight each other. The many colorful varieties are popular aquarium fish, however, the holding of the males in very small containers should be discouraged (Ref. 1672 ). Aquarium keeping: sexes should be kept separate unless for mating, and that only one female should be brought int

Trichopodus trichopterus.title: Trichopodus trichopterus, Three spot gourami : fisheries, aquaculture, aquarium
Trichopodus trichopterus.ecology: Freshwater; benthopelagic; pH range: 6.0 - 8.0; dH range: 5 - 19; potamodromous (Ref. 51243 ). Tropical; 22°C - 28°C (Ref. 1672 ); 26°N - 10°N, 99°E - 108°E
Trichopodus trichopterus.distribution: | Faunafri Asia: Mekong basin in Laos, Yunnan, Thailand, Cambodia and Viet Nam; Southeast Asia (Ref. 27732 ). Introduced elsewhere (Ref. 2847 ).
Trichopodus trichopterus.biology: Obligate air-breathing (Ref. 126274 ); Lives in lowland wetlands (Ref. 57235 ), in marshes, swamps and canals (Ref. 43281 ), with shallow sluggish or standing-water with a lot of aquatic vegetation. Occurs in seasonally flooded forests throughout the middle and lower Mekong (Ref. 12693 ). Undertakes lateral migrations from the Mekong mainstream, or other permanent water bodies, to flooded areas during the flood season and returns to the permanent water bodies at the onset of the dry season (Ref. 37770 ). An air-breathing species (Ref. 118402 ). Feeds on zooplankton, crustaceans and insect larv

Trichogaster lalius.title: Trichogaster lalius, Dwarf gourami : fisheries, aquarium
Trichogaster lalius.ecology: Freshwater; benthopelagic; pH range: 6.0 - 8.0; dH range: 5 - 19. Tropical; 25°C - 28°C (Ref. 2060 )
Trichogaster lalius.distribution: | Faunafri Asia: Pakistan, India and Bangladesh.
Trichogaster lalius.biology: Facultative air-breathing (Ref. 126274 ); Inhabits slow moving streams, rivulets and lakes with plenty of vegetation (Ref. 41236 ). An air-breathing species (Ref. 118402 ). Aquarium keeping: minimum aquarium size 60 cm (Ref. 51539 ).

Poecilia reticulata.title: Poecilia reticulata, Guppy : aquarium
Poecilia reticulata.ecology: Freshwater; brackish; benthopelagic; pH range: 7.0 - 8.0; dH range: 9 - 19; non-migratory (Ref. 126106 ). Tropical; 18°C - 28°C (Ref. 1672 ); 14°N - 2°N, 67°W - 52°W
Poecilia reticulata.distribution: | Faunafri South America: Venezuela, Barbados, Trinidad, northern Brazil and the Guyanas. Widely introduced and established elsewhere, mainly for mosquito control, but had rare to non-existing effects on mosquitoes, and negative to perhaps neutral effects on native fishes (Ref. 12217 ). Africa: Feral populations reported from the coastal reaches of
Poecilia reticulata.biology: Adults inhabit warm springs and their effluents, weedy ditches and canals (Ref. 5723 ). They are found in various habitats, ranging from highly turbid water in ponds, canals and ditches at low elevations to pristine mountain streams at high elevations (Ref. 11225 ). They occur in wide variety of habitats with low predation pressure, usually in very small streams and densely vegetated lakes and springs (Ref. 59043 ). Their salinity range is wide but requires fairly warm temperatures (23-24 °C) and quiet vegetated water for survival (Ref. 7248 , 44894 , 79840 ). They feed on zooplankton, small i

Poecilia sphenops.title: Poecilia sphenops, Molly : aquarium
Poecilia sphenops.ecology: Freshwater; brackish; benthopelagic; pH range: 7.5 - 8.2; dH range: 11 - 30; non-migratory (Ref. 126106 ). Tropical; 18°C - 28°C (Ref. 13371 ); 24°N - 1°S, 101°W - 69°W
Poecilia sphenops.distribution: | Faunafri Central and South America: Mexico to Colombia. Often confused with Poecilia mexicana (Ref. 1739 ).
Poecilia sphenops.biology: Adults feed on worms, crustaceans, insects, plant matter. The black variety (Black molly) is a very popular aquarium fish and is marketed throughout the world (Ref. 1739 ). In the aquarium it feeds on green algae and also readily accepts dried food (Ref. 1672 ). Minimum aquarium size 60 cm (Ref. 51539 ).

Xiphophorus maculatus.title: Xiphophorus maculatus, Southern platyfish : aquarium
Xiphophorus maculatus.ecology: Freshwater; benthopelagic; pH range: 7.0 - 8.0; dH range: 9 - 19; non-migratory (Ref. 126106 ). Tropical; 18°C - 25°C (Ref. 1672 ); 23°N - 17°N, 99°W - 86°W
Xiphophorus maculatus.distribution: | Faunafri North and Central America: Ciudad Veracruz, Mexico to northern Belize. At least one country reports adverse ecological impact after introduction.
Xiphophorus maculatus.biology: Adults occur in warm springs, canals and ditches with typically slow-moving water, silt bottoms and weedy banks (Refs. 5723; 44091, 44894 ). Also inhabit creeks and swamps (Ref. 44894 ). They feed on worms, crustaceans, insects and plant matter (Refs. 7020; 44091). Used for genetic research (Ref. 4537 ). Several color varieties are popular aquarium fishes, where they attain sexual maturity after 3-4 months and reproduce easily (Ref. 1672 ). Aquarium keeping: minimum aquarium size 60 cm (Ref. 51539 ).

Xiphophorus hellerii.title: Xiphophorus hellerii, Green swordtail : fisheries, aquarium
Xiphophorus hellerii.ecology: Freshwater; brackish; benthopelagic; pH range: 7.0 - 8.0; dH range: 9 - 19; non-migratory (Ref. 126106 ). Tropical; 22°C - 28°C (Ref. 52054 ); 26°N - 12°N
Xiphophorus hellerii.distribution: | Faunafri North and Central America: Rio Nantla, Veracruz in Mexico to northwestern Honduras. Africa: Feral populations reported from Natal and eastern Transvaal as well as in Lake Otjikoto, Namibia (Ref. 7248 ). Several countries report adverse ecological impact after introduction.
Xiphophorus hellerii.biology: Adults are found mainly in rapidly flowing streams and rivers, preferring heavily vegetated habitats (Ref. 26130 ). They occur in warm springs and their effluents, weedy canals and ponds (Ref. 5723 ). They feed on worms, crustaceans, insects and plant matter (Ref. 7020 ). Used for genetics research (Ref. 4537 ). Especially the red varieties are very popular aquarium fishes (Ref. 1672 ). Aquarium keeping: the males aggressive towards each other; minimum aquarium size 80 cm (Ref. 51539 ).

Corydoras paleatus.title: Hoplisoma paleatum, Peppered corydoras : aquarium
Corydoras paleatus.ecology: Freshwater; demersal; pH range: 6.0 - 8.0; dH range: 5 - 19. Subtropical; 18°C - 23°C (Ref. 30491 )
Corydoras paleatus.distribution: | Faunafri South America: Argentina, Brazil, and Uruguay.
Corydoras paleatus.biology: Facultative air-breathing (Ref. 126274 ); Found in ponds (Ref. 11229 ). Feeds on worms, crustaceans, insects and plant matter (Ref. 7020 ). Aquarium keeping: in groups of 5 or more individuals; minimum aquarium size 60 cm (Ref. 51539 ).

Corydoras aeneus.title: Osteogaster aenea, Bronze corydoras : aquarium
Corydoras aeneus.ecology: Freshwater; demersal; pH range: 6.0 - 8.0; dH range: 5 - 19; non-migratory (Ref. 126106 ). Subtropical; 25°C - 28°C (Ref. 30491 )
Corydoras aeneus.distribution: | Faunafri South America: Colombia and Trinidad to La Plata River basin east of the Andes.
Corydoras aeneus.biology: Facultative air-breathing (Ref. 126274 ); Found mostly in quiet, shallow waters with soft bottoms (Ref. 26041 ), but also inhabit running waters (Ref. 11225 ). Benthic (Ref. 58302 ). Adults stay in schools of 20 to 30 individuals. Because of their ability to breathe air intestinally, they take air 1 to 45 times per hour (Ref. 35381 ). Nocturnal (Ref. 35381 ). Adults feed on worms, crustaceans, insects and plant matter (Ref. 7020 ). Spawning occurs when the physical-chemical quality of the water changes with the onset of the rainy season (Ref. 35381 ). Aquarium keeping: in groups of 5 or more i

Corydoras sterbai.title: Hoplisoma sterbai, Sterba's cory : fisheries, aquarium
Corydoras sterbai.ecology: Freshwater; demersal; pH range: 6.0 - 8.0; dH range: 2 - 25. Tropical; 21°C - 25°C (Ref. 26041 )
Corydoras sterbai.distribution: | Faunafri South America: central Brazil and Bolivia.
Corydoras sterbai.biology: Facultative air-breathing (Ref. 126274 ); Found in smaller rivers and tributaries, as well as flooded forest pools with soft, acidic waters. The habitats are characterised by swift flowing water with few plants.

Corydoras panda.title: Hoplisoma panda, Panda corydoras : aquarium
Corydoras panda.ecology: Freshwater; demersal; pH range: 6.0 - 8.0; dH range: 2 - 25. Tropical; 20°C - 25°C (Ref. 2060 )
Corydoras panda.distribution: | Faunafri South America: Upper Amazon River basin.

Macrotocinclus affinis.title: Otocinclus affinis, Golden otocinclus : fisheries, aquarium
Macrotocinclus affinis.ecology: Freshwater; demersal; pH range: 6.0 - 8.0; dH range: 5 - 19. Tropical; 20°C - 26°C (Ref. 1672 )
Macrotocinclus affinis.distribution: | Faunafri South America: vicinity of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.
Macrotocinclus affinis.biology: Facultative air-breathing in the genus (Ref. 126274 ); Mainly nocturnal. Feeds on algae (Ref. 6868 ). Aquarium keeping: feeds on plants and roots; in groups of 5 or more individuals; minimum aquarium size 60 cm (Ref. 51539 ).

Pterygoplichthys pardalis.title: Pterygoplichthys pardalis, Amazon sailfin catfish : fisheries, aquarium
Pterygoplichthys pardalis.ecology: Freshwater; demersal; pH range: 7.0 - 7.5; dH range: 10 - 20. Tropical; 23°C - 28°C (Ref. 13614 )
Pterygoplichthys pardalis.distribution: | Faunafri South America: Lower, middle and upper Amazon River basin. Introduced to countries outside its native range.

Ancistrus cirrhosus.title: Ancistrus cirrhosus
Ancistrus cirrhosus.distribution: | Faunafri South America: Paraná River basin.
Ancistrus cirrhosus.biology: Facultative or obligate air-breathing (Ref. 126274 ); Inhabits streams, from highly turbid standing water over a heavy clay substratum to free flowing clear water over gravel. Algae-eater (Ref. 6868 ).

Pangasianodon hypophthalmus.title: Pangasianodon hypophthalmus, Striped catfish : fisheries, aquaculture, aquarium
Pangasianodon hypophthalmus.ecology: Freshwater; benthopelagic; pH range: 6.5 - 7.5; dH range: 2 - 29; potamodromous (Ref. 138296 ). Tropical; 22°C - 26°C (Ref. 13371 ); 19°N - 8°N
Pangasianodon hypophthalmus.distribution: | Faunafri Asia: Mekong, Chao Phraya, and Maeklong basins. Introduced into additional river basins for aquaculture.
Pangasianodon hypophthalmus.biology: Facultative air-breathing (Ref. 126274 ); Adults inhabit large rivers (Ref. 12693 ). Recorded as having been or being farmed in rice fields (Ref. 119549 ). Omnivorous (Ref. 6459 ), feeding on fish and crustaceans as well as on vegetable debris (Ref. 12693 ). A migratory species, moving upstream of the Mekong from unknown rearing areas to spawn in unknown areas in May-July and returning to the mainstream when the river waters fall seeking rearing habitats in September -December (Ref. 37772 ). South of the Khone Falls, upstream migration occurs from October to February, with peak in November-Dec

Pangasianodon gigas.title: Pangasianodon gigas, Mekong giant catfish : fisheries, aquaculture
Pangasianodon gigas.distribution: | Faunafri Asia: endemic to the Mekong basin where it has become rare due to overexploitation.
Pangasianodon gigas.biology: Facultative air-breathing (Ref. 126274 ); A migratory species (Ref. 37772 ) which occurs in medium to large-sized rivers (Ref. 12975 ). Adults feed on detritus and algae on the bottom (Ref. 58784 ); feeds only on vegetation in the river but takes other food in captivity; little is known on its general pattern of life and migratory journeys for spawning (Ref. 2686 ). Shows one of the fastest growth rates of any fish in the world, reaching 150 to 200 kg in 6 years (Ref. 12693 ). Cited in the Guinness Book of Records as largest freshwater fish (Ref. 6472 ). Marketed fresh (Ref. 12693 ). Maximum l

Silurus asotus.title: Silurus asotus, Amur catfish : fisheries, aquaculture, gamefish
Silurus asotus.distribution: | Faunafri Asia: Honshu, Shikoku and Kyushu in Japan, the Korean Peninsula, Taiwan, China, and Russia.
Silurus asotus.biology: Commercially cultured in Japan. Adults feed on all types of fish (Ref. 41072 ). Recorded as having been or being farmed in rice fields (Ref. 119549 ).

Channa argus.title: Channa argus, Snakehead : fisheries, aquaculture, gamefish, aquarium
Channa argus.distribution: | Faunafri Asia: Amur southward to Xi Jiang and Hainan Island, China (Ref. 82587 ). Introduced elsewhere. Japan (Ref. 6094 ) and the USA (Ref. 51238 ) report adverse ecological impact after introduction.
Channa argus.biology: Obligate air-breathing (Ref. 126274 ); Individuals can stay out of the water for 3 to 4 days at temperatures ranging from 10 to 15°C (Ref. 37350 ). They are typical ambush predators that lie waiting for prey on the bottom. They hunt mainly in the morning and in the evening, feeding primarily on fish (Ref. 12569 ). They mature at the age of 2 years and length of 30 cm. Spawning takes place in June and July (Ref. 56557 ). Eggs are pelagic. Utilized for human consumption.

Channa micropeltes.title: Channa micropeltes, Indonesian snakehead : fisheries, aquaculture, gamefish, aquarium
Channa micropeltes.ecology: Freshwater; benthopelagic; non-migratory (Ref. 126106 ); depth range 100 - ? m (Ref. 27732 ). Tropical; 25°C - 28°C (Ref. 1672 ); 10°N - 1°N, 95°E - 141°E
Channa micropeltes.distribution: | Faunafri Asia: Mekong and Chao Phraya basins; the Malay Peninsula, and the islands of Sumatra and Borneo. Material from India usually referred to as this species actually represents a distinct species.
Channa micropeltes.biology: Obligate air-breathing (Ref. 126274 ); Adults occur in lowland river and swamp (Ref. 57235 ). Usually associated with deep water bodies (Ref. 27732 ). They are found in large streams and canals (Ref. 4833 ), with standing or slowly flowing water (Ref. 12693 ). They feed mainly on fish but also takes some crustaceans. Spawns in small streams with dense vegetation (Ref. 56749 ). Utilized as a food fish (Ref. 4931 ). Economic important mainly from capture fisheries (Ref. 57235 ).

Polypterus senegalus.title: Polypterus senegalus, Gray bichir : fisheries
Polypterus senegalus.ecology: Freshwater; demersal; pH range: 6.0 - 8.0; dH range: 5 - 19; potamodromous (Ref. 51243 ). Tropical; 25°C - 28°C (Ref. 2060 ); 16°N - 2°S, 17°W - 37°E
Polypterus senegalus.distribution: | Faunafri Africa: subspecies Polypterus senegalus senegalus known from West Africa, in Senegal, Gambia, Niger, Volta and Chad basins (Ref. 2835 , 3188 , 81263 ), up to Nile River basin (Ref. 2835 , 3188 ) and lakes Turkana (Ref. 3188 ) and Albert (Ref. 41590 , 48922 , 48960 ). Subspecies Polypterus senegalus meridionalis known from middle and uppe
Polypterus senegalus.biology: Facultative air-breathing (Ref. 126274 ); This species inhabits marginal swamps and freshwater lagoons (Ref. 3066 ) and it appears to favor sheltered inshore habitats (Ref. 3034 ); it inhabits the muddy regions at the sides of rivers and swampy waters, where it lies quiet or glides about with snake-like movements (Ref. 49805 ). During the hottest hours of the day, it comes to the surface just on the outer edge of the vegetation, and it goes back to the bottom when disturbed (Ref. 45962 ). Atractosteus spatula.title: Atractosteus spatula, Alligator gar : fisheries, gamefish, aquarium
Atractosteus spatula.ecology: Freshwater; brackish; demersal; potamodromous (Ref. 126106 ); depth range 0 - ? m (Ref. 55223 ). Subtropical; 44°N - 20°N, 101°W - 82°W (Ref. 55223 )
Atractosteus spatula.distribution: | Faunafri North America: ranges from Mississippi River basin from southwestern Ohio and southern Illinois in USA south to Gulf of Mexico; Gulf of Mexico Coastal Plain from Enconfina River in Florida, USA to Veracruz, Mexico.
Atractosteus spatula.biology: Facultative air-breathing (Ref. 126274 ); Adults inhabit sluggish pools and backwaters of large rivers, swamps, bayous, and lakes. Rarely enter brackish and marine waters (Ref. 5723 ). They feed on blue crabs, turtles, waterfowl or other birds and small mammals (Ref. 10294 ). Giant of the gars (Ref. 5723 ). Marketed fresh (Ref. 37032 ).

Scleropages formosus.title: Scleropages formosus, Asian bonytongue : fisheries, aquarium
Scleropages formosus.distribution: | Faunafri Asia: Southern Myanmar to Malay Peninsula and Indonesia, eastern Thailand to Cardamon Range.
Scleropages formosus.biology: Occurs in tannin stained blackwater streams (Ref. 12693 ). Found in forest covered streams including peat adjacent areas. Take around three months for free swimming fries (Ref. 57235 ). Young individuals feed on insects at the water surface, adults take fishes (Ref. 12693 , 57235 ) and smaller vertebrates (Ref. 56749 ). A mouth brooder, young about 6 cm at birth (Ref. 7050 , 57235 ). Valued as an aquarium fish, its flesh commands a moderate price.

Stenopus hispidus.title: Stenopus hispidus, Banded coral shrimp : fisheries
Stenopus hispidus.distribution: Indo-Pacific and Western Atlantic: From the Red Sea and South Africa to Tuamotu Is., Hawaii and Easter Is. In the Atlantic: North Carolina and Bermuda to the Caribbean Sea and south to São Paulo, Brazil. Tropical and subtropical.
Stenopus hispidus.biology: Maximum depth from Ref. 97531 . Subtidal (Ref. 106854 ). Found on rocky bottoms and coral reefs (Ref. 83922 ). Also occur at natural depressions in rock formations (Ref. 126252 ). General carnivore (Ref. 116259 ). Feed mainly on small arthropods and other marine invertebrates. Considered as a cleaner shrimp, removing and consuming parasites, injured tissue, and leftover food particles from other reef fishes (Ref. 125532 ). Dwells in deep crevices and reef overhangs (Ref. 129713 ).

Panulirus japonicus.title: Panulirus japonicus, Japanese spiny lobster : fisheries
Panulirus japonicus.biology: It has lengths of 30 cm, maximum total body length; 25 cm, common length (Ref. 4 ). Occurs in depths between 1 and 15 m on rocky bottoms and inhabits shallow waters (Ref. 4 ).

Macrocheira kaempferi.title: Macrocheira kaempferi, Japanese giant spider crab
Macrocheira kaempferi.ecology: Benthic; depth range 50 - 400 m (Ref. 99853 ), usually 50 - 200 m (Ref. 99852 ). Subtropical
Macrocheira kaempferi.biology: Largest crab in the world. Leg span may measure up to 3.7 m and weight may exceed more than 13.6 kg (Ref. 99323 ).

Oncorhynchus mykiss.title: Oncorhynchus mykiss, Rainbow trout : fisheries, aquaculture, gamefish
Oncorhynchus mykiss.ecology: Marine; freshwater; brackish; benthopelagic; anadromous (Ref. 138269 ); depth range 0 - 200 m (Ref. 50550 ). Subtropical; 10°C - 24°C (Ref. 12741 ); 67°N - 32°N, 135°E - 117°W
Oncorhynchus mykiss.distribution: | Faunafri Pacific Slope from Kuskokwim River drainage in Alaska to Otay River drainage in California, USA. Widely introduced and established in Canada and USA, including Arctic, Atlantic, Great Lakes, Mississippi River, and Rio Grande basins, and elsewhere in the world (Ref. 86798 ). Oncorhynchus mykiss.biology: Inhabit clear, cold headwaters, creeks, small to large rivers, lakes, and intertidal areas (Ref. 86798 ). Anadromous in coastal streams (Ref. 5723 ). Stocked in almost all water bodies as lakes, rivers and streams, usually not stocked in water reaching summer temperatures above 25°C or ponds with very low oxygen concentrations. Feed on a variety of aquatic and terrestrial invertebrates and small fishes. At the sea, they prey on fish and cephalopods. Mature individuals undertake short spawning migrations. Clibanarius tricolor.title: Clibanarius tricolor, Tricolor hermit : fisheries
Clibanarius tricolor.distribution: Western Atlantic Ocean and Caribbean Sea.

Oncorhynchus keta.title: Oncorhynchus keta, Chum salmon : fisheries, aquaculture, gamefish, aquarium
Oncorhynchus keta.ecology: Marine; freshwater; brackish; benthopelagic; anadromous (Ref. 132363 ); depth range 0 - 250 m (Ref. 50550 ), usually ? - 61 m (Ref. 96339 ). Temperate; 0°C - 24°C (Ref. 35682 ); 67°N - 24°N, 130°E - 110°W (Ref. 117423 )
Oncorhynchus keta.distribution: | Faunafri North Pacific: Korea , Japan, Okhotsk and Bering Sea (Ref. 1998 ), Arctic Alaska south to San Diego, California, USA. Asia: Iran (Ref. 39702 ).
Oncorhynchus keta.biology: Inhabits ocean and coastal streams (Ref. 86798 ). Migrating fry form schools in estuaries, remain close to shore for a few months and finally disperse to enter the sea (Ref. 1998 ). Epipelagic (Ref. 58426 ). Juveniles and adults feed mainly on copepods, tunicates and euphausiids but also on pteropods, squid and small fishes (Ref. 1998 ). Adults cease feeding in freshwater (Ref. 1998 ). Males and females die after spawning. The catch is mostly canned but also sold fresh, dried-salted, smoked, and frozen. Eaten steamed, fried, broiled, boiled, microwaved, and baked (Ref. 9988 ). Portunus trituberculatus.title: Portunus trituberculatus, Gazami crab : fisheries
Portunus trituberculatus.ecology: Benthopelagic; depth range 0 - 100 m (Ref. 132434 ). Tropical, preferred 24°C (Ref. 107945 ); 42°N - 38°S, 79°E - 154°E (Ref. 106948 )
Portunus trituberculatus.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: from Honshu, Japan, west to eastern India and Sri Lanka, and south to New South Wales, Australia.
Portunus trituberculatus.biology: Minimum depth assumed from its ecology. Shallow waters up to depths of 50 m. Inhabits sandy to sandy-muddy substrates (Ref. 343 ). Benthopelagic predator, feeding mainly on bivalves (Lamellibranchia), benthic crustaceans, fishes and cephalopods (Ref. 117071 ).

Pygocentrus nattereri.title: Pygocentrus nattereri, Red piranha : fisheries, gamefish, aquarium
Pygocentrus nattereri.ecology: Freshwater; pelagic; pH range: 5.5 - 7.5; dH range: ? - 20; potamodromous (Ref. 126106 ). Subtropical; 23°C - 27°C (Ref. 13371 ); 9°N - 34°S
Pygocentrus nattereri.distribution: | Faunafri South America: Amazon River basin, Paraguay-Paraná River basin, northeastern Brazilian coastal rivers and Essequibo River basin (Ref. 39031 ). Reported from the Uruguay River, Brazil (Ref. 79585 ).
Pygocentrus nattereri.biology: Common in creeks and interconnected ponds in Matto Grosso, Brazil, where it influences distribution and feeding of other fish (Ref. 9080 ) and in areas of high primary production in Rio Machado and Rio Negro (Ref.9096). Adults feed mainly at dusk and dawn on insects, worms and fish (Ref. 7020 ). Medium-sized to large individuals (15-24 cm length) forage mainly at dawn, late afternoon and night up to about 2200H, whereas smaller fish (8-11 cm) are active mainly during the day (Ref. 9080 ). Electrophorus electricus.title: Electrophorus electricus, Electric eel : fisheries, gamefish, aquarium
Electrophorus electricus.distribution: | Faunafri South America: restricted to the Guiana Shield.
Electrophorus electricus.biology: Prefer muddy bottoms and calm waters; frequently found in coastal plains, swamps and creeks but is also found inland where a favorable biotope exist. Juveniles feed on invertebrates, adults feed on fish and small mammals (Ref. 12225 ), first-born larvae prey on other eggs and embryos coming from late spawning batches (Ref. 40645 ). The electric organ of this species consists of flattened electrocytes, numbering to about hundreds of thousands, connected in series (Ref. 10840 ; 10011 ). Chromodoris annae.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: Malaysia to Marshall Islands.

Chromodoris lochi.biology: Assumed maximum length from Ref. 844 . Feeds on sponges (Ref. 844 ).

Acanthaster planci.title: Acanthaster planci, Crown-of-thorns
Acanthaster planci.biology: Minimum depth from Ref. 81548 . Cryptic on coral areas (Also Ref. 129602 ) and reef patches (Ref. 78188 ). On a reef slope (Ref. 97449 ). Feeds on hard corals, soft corals, encrusting organisms, algae, gorgonians and cannibalistic on other Acanthaster planci (Ref. 78188 ). Nocturnal (Ref. 130720 ).

Linckia laevigata.title: Linckia laevigata, Blue linckia
Linckia laevigata.biology: Occurs in shallow reef areas exposed to the sunlight, on rocks, dead coral or rubble at depths of 0 to 60 m (Ref. 800 ). Also on a reef slope (Ref. 97449 ); among sponges, macroalgae and seagrasses (Ref. 82802 ). Juveniles hide under corals and rocks. Feeds on detritus, small invertebrates living on algal mats and dead animals (Ref. 800 ). Associated with coral communities. Likely feeds on turf algae and bacterial film over hard substrates (Ref. 129602 ).

Diadema setosum.title: Diadema setosum, Porcupine sea urchin
Diadema setosum.distribution: Indo-Pacific: from Red Sea to South Pacific Islands and Japan. Introduced in the Mediterranean.
Diadema setosum.biology: Common in the sublittoral fringe around protected rocky coastlines (Ref. 102838 ). Found on muddy substrate (Ref. 2931 ). Occurs in assemblages in reef areas with high percentage of dead corals (Ref. 800 ). Common on Porites -dominated coral reefs; less common on Acropora assemblage (Ref. 102838 ). Feeds on algae (Also Ref. 128613 ) that grows on dead corals or rubble area (Ref. 800 ). Dwells in rocky and sandy substrates at depths of 1-70m. Also inhabits coral reefs and sea grass meadows. Octopus cyanea.title: Octopus cyanea, Big blue octopus : fisheries
Octopus cyanea.distribution: Indo-Pacific: from eastern Africa to Hawaiian Islands.
Octopus cyanea.biology: Shallow-water benthic species inhabiting coral reefs and found in a variety of substrata (Ref. 81543 ). Occupies lairs in coral bedrock, live and dead coral heads and excavations in sand and rubble (Ref. 96968 ). In naturally-occurring holes on rocks or dens (Ref. 81543 ). Males and females can occupy adjacent dens (Ref. 96968 ). Juveniles rapidly form homes and defend these against conspecifics (Ref. 105171 ). Thaumoctopus mimicus.biology: Mantle length is 5.8 cm. Species is known for its mimicry of toxic models that co-occur in the same habitat, namely banded soles, sea snakes, and lionfish, with other distinct postures and behaviors currently being open to interpretation (Ref. 96968 ). This octopus often occupies the vacated burrows of other animals. These lairs appear temporary or may form a network of regular lairs within a home range. Enteroctopus dofleini.title: Enteroctopus dofleini, North Pacific giant octopus : fisheries, bait
Enteroctopus dofleini.distribution: Indo-Pacific and Northwest Atlantic: from Baja California northwest to Alaska and west to Japan. Tropical to boreal.
Enteroctopus dofleini.biology: World's largest octopus species (Refs. 106261 , 106263 ). It's mantle length is to at least 60 cm (Ref. 96968 ). Common weight: 2,000 to 10,000 g (Ref. 275 ). Females grow larger than males (Ref. 3722 ). Radial spread may measure up to 9.8 m (Ref. 99323 ). Not found in the deep, open ocean (Ref. 106263 ). It is found on rocky and soft bottoms near a home crevice or cave (Ref. 865 ) from the low intertidal (Refs. 865 , 275 ), to a depth of 180 meters (Ref. 865 ). Sepioteuthis lessoniana.title: Sepioteuthis lessoniana, Bigfin reef squid : fisheries
Sepioteuthis lessoniana.ecology: Demersal; brackish; depth range 0 - 100 m (Ref. 275 ). Tropical; 51°N - 48°S, 22°E - 155°W (Ref. 106950 )

Sepioteuthis lessoniana.biology: Also caught by set nets and spears and jigs. Demersal neritic species (Ref. 105081 ). Inhabits warm coastal waters (Ref. 101164 ). Mastigias papua.title: Mastigias papua, Papuan jellyfish
Mastigias papua.distribution: Indo-West Pacific: from South Africa north to Russia and east to Fiji. Tropical to temperate.
Mastigias papua.biology: Mostly in shallow waters during the day to allow its symbiotic zooxanthellae (where it derives its energy from) to bathe in sunlight. Mainly solitary. As the sun mainly influences its habits, it descends to lower parts of the water column when the sun sets. It gathers food such as zooplankton, phytoplankton, small invertebrates, and microbes using the oral arms of its mouth (Ref. 101744 ).

Cotylorhiza tuberculata.title: Cotylorhiza tuberculata
Cotylorhiza tuberculata.distribution: Mediterranean Sea: Italy, Greece and Monaco.

Feeds on fine plankton, which is absorbed by the oral arms (Ref. 358 ).

Eretmochelys imbricata.ecology: Reef-associated; brackish; depth range 0 - 300 m (Ref. 102845 ). Tropical; 24°C - 31°C (Ref. 138175 ); 52°N - 56°S, 118°W - 124°W
Eretmochelys imbricata.distribution: Indo-Pacific and the Atlantic Ocean. Stray in the Mediterreanean Sea.
Eretmochelys imbricata.biology: The most tropical of all sea turtles living in littoral waters. Turtles measuring up to 10 cm straight carapace length are usually nektonic animal. A carnivorous turtle commonly poking in crevices between rocks and corals; it becomes a regular inhabitant of hard substrata, i.e., corals, tunicates, algae and sponges. The duration of incubation lasts 47 to 75 days but varies depending on place and time. It is a high valued species in the international market (Ref. 1397 ). Caretta caretta.biology: Migratory (Ref. 417 ). Inhabits shallow thermocline at 50 m with strong thermal and chlorophyll gradients and surface convergent fronts (Ref. 78527 ), continental shores of warm seas and common in shallow waters (Ref. 1397 ) and brackish water estuaries (Ref. 417 ). Feed widely on variety of invertebrates especially bony fishes (Ref. 804 ). Nesting grounds associated with underwater "refuges": crevices in rocky or reef points, near to the nesting beaches. Dermochelys coriacea.title: Dermochelys coriacea, Leatherback turtle : fisheries
Dermochelys coriacea.ecology: Benthopelagic; depth range 0 - 1250 m (Ref. 78668 ), usually 0 - 200 m (Ref. 78668 ). Tropical; 72°N - 49°S, 180°W - 180°E (Ref. 1397 )
Dermochelys coriacea.biology: Deepest dive recorded based on Ref. 86780 , usually epipelagic (Refs. 78668 , 85378 ). They are commonly found in the upper 200 m (Ref. 85786 ). Hatchlings and juveniles are assumed to be pelagic, migrating in search of food. Adults mainly feed on pelagic invertebrates, e.g., jellyfishes, tunicates, crustaceans and juvenile fishes. In some places it is used as bait for long line shark fisheries but this species have no commercial fisheries (Ref. 1397 ), although pelagic fisheries has been identified as a major source of its mortality (Ref. 85378 ). Delphinus delphis.title: Delphinus delphis, Common dolphin : fisheries
Delphinus delphis.ecology: Pelagic-oceanic; oceanodromous (Ref. 75906 ); depth range 0 - 2000 m (Ref. 138071 ). Tropical; 10°C - 28°C (Ref. 75906 ); 90°N - 90°S, 180°W - 180°E
Delphinus delphis.distribution: Indo-Pacific, Atlantic Ocean and Mediterranean and Black Sea. Warm temperate and tropical waters. It is not reported in Antarctic territories (Ref. 128552 ) [Mediterranean population: IUCN 2010 (Ref. 84930 ): EN, A2abc.]

Commonly in large herds of 30 or more individuals (Ref. 801 ). Feeds on small schooling fish and squid; at night on creatures associated with the deep scattering layer (DSL), which migrates towards the surface in the dark (Ref. 1394 ). Preyed upon by great white sharks (Ref. 8891 ). Delphinus capensis tropicalis : They were reported to bow ride although not in areas particularly where hunting occurs. Phoca vitulina.title: Phoca vitulina, Harbour seal : fisheries

Feeds on a wide variety of fish, cephalopods, and crustaceans of surface, mid-water and benthic habitats (Ref. 1394 ). It is preyed upon by the great white shark (Ref. 32140 ). Megaptera novaeangliae.distribution: Circumglobal. [Arabian Sea population: EN, D; Oceania population: EN, A1ad: IUCN 2010 (Ref. 84930 )].
Megaptera novaeangliae.biology: They migrate from tropics (breeding areas) to polar or sub-polar regions, reaching the ice edges in both hemispheres (feeding areas); their migrations take them through oceanic zones (Ref. 1394 ). Maximum depth from Ref. 122827 . Feed and breed in coastal waters, often near human population centres, and this helps make them one of the most familiar of the large whales. Feeds on krill and small schooling fish (Ref. 1394 ). Potamotrygon motoro.title: Potamotrygon motoro, South American freshwater stingray : fisheries, gamefish, aquarium
